messages:
Maya: heads-up — saw memory climbing on a few long-context workloads when continuous-batching merges small groups. repro on stage with seq_len=12k, concurrency=40. flamegraph attached (snippet below).

Maya: flamegraph top: kv_cache::page_fetch ~45% -> kv_cache::merge_batches ~18% -> gpu_send_wait ~10%

Maya: repro command: `./run_perf --workload longctx --seq 12000 --concurrency 40 --batching continuous --kv-enabled`

Juan: can you paste the perf counters? is this paging or refcount churn?

Maya: counters: page_allocs/sec +2.1k, page_evictions/sec +480, avg_page_size 64KB, kvcache_hits 78%, kvcache_misses 22% (higher than baseline).

Eli: looks like fragmentation + repeated merges cause head-of-line stalls: merged batch holds head slot while waiting for other fragments -> other batches queue.

Sophie: do we have a short trace (span ids) showing which path holds the slot?

Maya: short trace (sampler):
```
span: request|batch=12|ctx=A -> kvcache:fetch_page -> merge_batches:attempt -> wait_for_fragments (120ms) -> gpu_submit
span: request|batch=8|ctx=B -> blocked_on: head_slot(A)
```

Juan: 120ms wait is big. Why are merges waiting that long? network/gpu slow?

Maya: not network. root cause seems to be merge policy that waits up to merge_timeout=100ms for small fragments to coalesce; with longctx we get many long sequences that produce small fragments at tail and timeout keeps head slot reserved.

Eli: rough idea: change policy to prefer local-forward merge (only merge fragments from same ctx) or fall back to immediate split when head queue length > N. That reduces cross-ctx HOL.

Sophie: adding metric `kvcache.merge_wait_ms{ctx}` and `kvcache.head_hold_count` would help alert. Also add per-route merge drop rate so we can tune threshold per model.

Maya: tried a quick patch on stage: if head_hold > 3 then set merge_timeout=15ms for new attempts. result: p99 latency down 35% for those requests, mem growth stops after warmup.

Eli: interesting. any regression on throughput?

Maya: throughput stable, tokens/s +-2%. small uptick in GPU submit calls but batching still effective.

Juan: we should also look at kernel selection: larger merged batches triggered a fallback to the generic attention kernel which uses more scratch mem. If we avoid big cross-ctx merges we stay on optimized kernel. That explains memory delta.

Sophie: good catch. can we add a heuristic: if merge would change kernel class (fast->generic) then abort merge?

Eli: yeah: compute predicted_kernel(batch_shape) cheaply and skip merge if kernel_class changes. cheap check.

Maya: opened PR with two changes: 1) adaptive short-circuit merge when head_hold high, 2) kernel-class-aware merge veto. staging tests + perf.

deploy-bot: maya/PR #4123 merged into staging — CI passed (unit + integration), will run perf job 1:00h.

Juan: long-term, we should re-evaluate page_eviction watermarking and fragmentation compaction: maybe proactive coalescing when idle. but short-term the merge-veto + metrics is a good safety net.

Sophie: created dashboard tile for `kvcache.merge_wait_ms` and `kvcache.vetoed_merges` and alert if merge_wait_ms_p95 > 50ms for 5m.

Maya: leaving the stage perf job running; will post final numbers tomorrow. thanks all :raised_hands:

Eli: if the stage job looks good, can we canary to prod-dedicated with low traffic? want to validate kernel-class logic on real models.

Maya: yes — plan: canary next Wed 2am PT, 5% traffic to cluster redwood-east-2-dedicated-1.

Juan: note to self: add a small unit test for predicted_kernel and a fuzz test to ensure merge veto doesn't starve longctx.

Maya: added ticket: RW-1189 for fuzz + compaction followup.

Sophie: thanks — will sync on runbook updates for oncall.

Maya: end.
